newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST - Polish repo/revrepo seen down by end-97.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Polish repo/revrepo seen down by end-97.

text.p: Banks expect liquidity on the money market would shrink towards the end of this year, prompting repo operations alongside the current reverse repos, a Reuters poll of Poland's 24 biggest banks showed.
Banks predicted the National Bank of Poland's 14-day revrepo rate, last at 21.64 percent, would fall to 17.84 percent by year-end.
The forecast is a mean average of banks' predictions ranging from 16.25 to 20.00 percent. @

Banks expected the reverse repo rate to ease to 21.57 percent on average this month with a range from 19.7 to 21.8 percent and to 17.43 percent in February 1998 with a range from 15.0 to 19.8 percent.
However, seven of the polled banks expected the central bank would stage both reverse repo and repo operations or only repos at the end of the year.
The repo rate at the end of 1997 was seen at 18.84 percent on average with a range of predictions from 17.5 to 20.5 percent. @

Only five banks expected the central bank to do repos in February and their average predicted repo rate was 21.96 percent with a range of 21.60 to 22.64 percent and falling to 18.76 percent in 12 months time -- in February 1998 within a range of 17.4 to 20.5 percent.
